deep.reconstruction:
This page contains no mathematics. Folio 35v is not a Riemann manuscript page. It is the second (closing) page of a letter in German Kurrent script, signed 'ergebenst H. A. Schwarz, Weender Chaussee 2..' (Göttingen). Schwarz held the Göttingen chair from 1875.

Context: The recipient is the editor responsible for the posthumous edition of Riemann's memoir 'Über die Fläche vom kleinsten Inhalt bei gegebener Begrenzung'. That memoir was originally worked up from Riemann's papers by K. Hattendorff (1867). The letter concerns its reprinting, as a 'Separatabdruck' and in the context of Riemann's Gesammelte Werke (ed. H. Weber with R. Dedekind, 1876). The recipient is most plausibly Weber or Dedekind; I cannot settle which from this page.

Content of the page: Schwarz regrets that his letter brings unwelcome news. The trust and indulgence the recipient showed Herr Hattendorff have been poorly rewarded. Had Schwarz been able to see Hattendorff's manuscript beforehand, most of the passages he now has to object to could have been settled by more careful correction. Now the recipient faces a choice: justify larger changes to the publisher, or keep gross errors. Even the indispensable changes cannot be made 'im Handumdrehen' (in a flash). Schwarz exclaims that no one could have believed Hattendorff would take his task so little to heart. At least sending him the proof sheet ('Correcturbogen') had the good effect that the inaccuracies were noticed. He hopes the recipient will not bear him a grudge for having had the misfortune of discovering errors. The letter closes with greetings to the recipient's wife and children and New Year wishes, so it was written around the turn of 1875/76. It is followed by greetings involving a 'Schwager' (reading uncertain).

Relation to the next page: The next folio is Schwarz's follow-up letter of 24 January 1876. It shows the mathematical substance of the dispute:
- Schwarz objects to the phrase 'quadrirtes Linienelement' (squared line element).
- He objects to equations of the form log X = 2 log Y + const.
- His main objection is the unjustified inference on p. 25 of the offprint that 'the argument of Y changes by alpha*pi' at a corner of the boundary polygon. Schwarz asks how one knows that X - X0 is expandable in powers of Y - Y0 at a boundary corner.

None of that mathematics appears on 35v itself. There is therefore no derivation to reconstruct.
errors: No mathematical content on this page, so there are no mathematical errors to assess.
Historical note: the 'errors' Schwarz complains of are attributed to Hattendorff's editorial work, not to Riemann.

results.what: Editorial correspondence: H. A. Schwarz criticizes K. Hattendorff's edition of Riemann's minimal-surface memoir when it was reprinted (c. 1875/76, Gesammelte Werke / Separatabdruck).
results.modern_name: History of the editing of Riemann's 'Über die Fläche vom kleinsten Inhalt bei gegebener Begrenzung'
results.usually_credited_to: Letter by H. A. Schwarz; edition by K. Hattendorff (1867), later reprinted in Riemann's Werke (Weber/Dedekind, 1876)

deep.surprise_reason: The page is not by Riemann. It is a non-mathematical letter by H. A. Schwarz about editorial errors in Hattendorff's edition of Riemann's minimal-surface paper. It is of mild interest for the history of the Werke edition and Schwarz's critical role, but contains no mathematics attributable to Riemann.
transcription_corrections: The page is a letter in H. A. Schwarz's hand (signed 'H. A. Schwarz, Weender Chaussee 2..'), not a Riemann manuscript. The ink is very faint and many words are uncertain; the machine transcription's overall sense matches what is legible.
'Hattendorff' is the correct reading of the name in line 3 (confirmed by the next page).

In the closing, 'Ihrer Frau Gemahlin und Ihren Kindern ...' is likely followed by a phrase of the form 'empfehle ich mich bestens', though this is uncertain. The final greeting line containing 'Schwager' is uncertain and may refer to the writer's wife and brother-in-law/sister-in-law.
The isolated 'H. [?]' under the greeting line is more likely a flourish or abbreviation than a separate word; it is uncertain.
